parsed.why: No trans criminalisation, sodomy legal, courts repeatedly strike down restrictions and grant partnership and foreign-spouse rights; but documented public hostility, police failure on assembly, and weak hate-crime support keep it short of the acceptance tier.

Unenforced sodomy statute, no trans-specific offence or documented targeting, and a documented traditional gender-diverse role signal acceptance; thin, decade-old social data and open questions on current enforcement hold it a step below acceptance-with-protections.

X markers accepted, non-surgical gender recognition, hate-crime law covering gender identity, judicially enforced service equality and preference-based custody placement; residual documented night-time violence and one state's prison-placement divergence keep it below the top tier.

Enforced sodomy law with documented arrests of LGBTQ people after attacks, victims deterred from reporting, active pushes for harsher penalties, and documented concealment norm; one employment protection barely offsets a hostile criminal regime.

De-facto criminalisation of gender nonconformity itself under morality offences carrying five years, religious rulings barring care, no recognition or recourse, unregistrable organisations, plus documented militia torture and killings for effeminate presentation.
